A Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is available for up to a maximum of €50,000, including 
VAT, for refurbishment of vacant properties for use as a principle private residence or to be made 
available for rent, including the conversion of a property which has not been used as residential 
heretofore.   A top-up grant of up to €20,000 is also available for properties which are derelict.  
An on-line application system for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant was introduced in 
Laois County Council on 11th June 2026.   The new system will make it easier for applicants to 
apply, with all documentation and supporting resources stored within their own personal account.  
The new system will enhance the Council’s efficiency of application processing.  All new 
applications from must be submitted on-line only.

Vacant Above the Shop Grant 
A grant of up to €135,000 is available for the conversion or refurbishment of vacant above shop 
space into residential units for occupation as a principal private residence and/or for residential 
units), subject to appropriate planning permission being in place.  Where one residential unit is 
being created in the vacant above the shop space a grant of up to €95,000 will be available, where 
two residential units are being created up to €115,000 is available and where three or more units 
are created up to €135,000 is available. 
 
The Grant applies to vacant ‘above the shop’ space in buildings in cities, towns and villages, where 
the building was built prior to 2008 and the space/existing residential unit(s) have been vacant for 
two years or more prior to application. The ground floor commercial space may be vacant or in use 
at time of application but must be remaining in commercial use.  
 
Expert Advice Grant 
An Expert Advice Grant is available for Vacant Above the Shop Conversions and Conversion of 
former commercial / public use buildings to residential units.  The Expert Advice Grant provides 
funding of up to €5,000 towards having an appropriately qualified professional provide expert 
advice to the owner of;  
  
• 
A building with a commercial element and vacant above the shop space who may avail of 
the Vacant Above the Shop Grant to convert / refurbish the vacant space into residential 
unit/s, with the commercial element remaining. 
• 
A former vacant commercial / public use building who may avail of the Vacant Property 
Refurbishment Grant Conversion of former Commercial Building / public use building to 
convert the entire building into more than one residential unit. 
 
Only one Expert Advice grant can be applied for per building.  Applications can only be made by 
named individuals who own the building for which the advice grant is being applied, or who are 
actively engaged in purchasing the building. Where there is more than one owner of the building, 
all owners must be included on the application form. The Expert Advice Grant is not currently 
available to registered companies, developers, undertakings etc.

Midlands Flavours in Ballykilcavan Farm and Brewery on June 30th  
 
The Midlands Flavours Network Gathering, supported by Local Enterprise Office Laois and held at 
Ballykilcavan Farm and Brewery, brought together food and drink producers from across Laois and 
the wider Midlands region. The event provided valuable opportunities for networking, 
collaboration and knowledge sharing, while showcasing Laois’ strengths in agri-food, rural 
enterprise and food tourism. Presentations from industry experts and producer-led discussions 
helped inform and support the continued growth of the sector, reinforcing Laois’ reputation as a 
centre of excellence for food and drink production.

LEO Laois continued its programme of business support and engagement activities with a highly 
successful Lunch and Learn event hosted in Stradbally Library in June. The event was very well 
attended by local entrepreneurs, business owners and individuals considering starting a business, 
providing an opportunity to access practical business advice, network with peers and learn about 
the supports available through the Local Enterprise Office.  
 
 
Lisa Molloy, Head of Enterprise and Economic Development & Honor Deevy, Senior Enterprise Development Officer with attendees at the 
Stradbally Lunch and Learn Event  
 
Building on the strong interest and positive feedback received, the next Lunch and Learn event is 
scheduled to take place in the Market House Portarlington on 10th September, with further 
sessions planned in locations across the county. The initiative aims to improve accessibility to 
business supports, strengthen local enterprise networks and encourage entrepreneurship 
throughout County Laois. 
 
Borris-in-Ossory Courthouse Redevelopment: Enterprise, Economic 
Development and Community Engagement Event 
A well-attended Enterprise and Community Information Evening was held in St. Canice’s Hall, 
Borris-in-Ossory on 15 July, jointly hosted by Laois County Council and Local Enterprise Office 
Laois. The event provided local business owners, aspiring entrepreneurs, community groups and 
residents with an opportunity to learn about the range of business, enterprise and community 
supports available, engage directly with Council and LEO representatives, and network with others 
from across the local area. 
 
A key focus of the evening was the proposed redevelopment of the historic Courthouse building 
on Main Street as a modern Community and Digital Enterprise Hub. The project was positively 
received by attendees, who were provided with an update on the vision for the facility and the 
proposed redevelopment plans. The event also offered an opportunity for local groups, businesses 
and individuals to share ideas, discuss potential future uses of the building and explore how they 
can become involved in the development and operation of the hub. 
 
The consultation generated valuable feedback and marked the first in a series of engagement 
initiatives that will help shape the future use of the facility. Further information sessions and 
stakeholder engagement activities are planned over the coming months to gather expressions of 
interest from prospective users and ensure the project reflects local needs and opportunities.

that contribute to the social and cultural life of Portarlington. The PCDA office is open daily from

Canal Road Business Park, Portarlington – Official Opening 
The official opening of the Canal Road Business Park, Portarlington took place on 8 July, marking a 
significant milestone in the economic development of the town and wider County Laois. Developed 
by Laois County Council on a six-acre site formerly associated with the Avon Cosmetics facility, 
and supported through the EU Just Transition Fund, the project represents a strategic investment 
in enterprise infrastructure and sustainable regional growth. 
 
The development comprises four fully serviced enterprise sites designed to accommodate a 
diverse range of business activities, including manufacturing, technology, logistics and other 
growth sectors. By providing modern, development-ready enterprise space, the business park will 
support indigenous business expansion, attract new investment and create opportunities for 
employment growth within the region.

Laois Commuter Survey 2026 
The Laois Commuter Survey 2026, commissioned by Laois County Council and undertaken by 
Interactions Ltd during February and March 2026, has been completed and published. The survey 
provides valuable insights into commuting patterns, employment trends, travel behaviours and the 
experiences of workers living in County Laois. 
 
The publication of the survey represents an important resource for both the Council and key 
stakeholders, providing a robust evidence base to support strategic planning and future initiatives 
aimed at improving quality of life, reducing commuting pressures and strengthening the county’s 
economic competitiveness. 
 
The full report is available on the Invest Laois website: investlaois.ie/news/2026/laois-commuter-
survey-2026. 
 
Invest Laois Marketing Campaign 
The Invest Laois marketing campaign continues to promote County Laois as a leading location for 
business investment and enterprise growth. Through a series of business testimonials, 
promotional videos and targeted digital marketing initiatives, the campaign highlights the county’s 
strategic location, strong business ecosystem and quality of life.  
 
Extensive promotion across social media channels and the Invest Laois website has generated 
significant reach and engagement, helping to raise awareness of Laois as an attractive destination 
for indigenous business expansion and inward investment. 
 
Further information is available at www.investlaois.ie/why-choose-laois.

Farming for Nature Festival 
Laois County Council was pleased to provide grant support towards the recent Farming for Nature 
Festival, hosted at Ballykilcavan Farm and Brewery, Stradbally. The festival attracted farmers, 
researchers, food producers and environmental stakeholders from across Ireland, showcasing 
County Laois as a centre for innovation, sustainability and rural enterprise. Events such as this 
generate valuable economic activity for the county, enhance its reputation as a destination for agri-
food and rural development initiatives, and provide important opportunities for knowledge 
sharing, tourism and community engagement. 
 
An Dún Continues to Grow as a Key Cultural and Community Venue 
Since opening in July 2024, An Dún Performance & Events Space has become an important cultural 
and community venue for Portlaoise and County Laois. During 2026, it has hosted a diverse 
programme of events encompassing arts, music, culture, sport and community engagement, 
including Cruinniú na nÓg activities, performances by local schools and music groups, cultural 
celebrations, community festivals, Pride of Place initiatives and sporting events. The continued 
growth in usage demonstrates the versatility of the facility and its value in supporting community 
participation, cultural expression and recreational opportunities while enhancing the social and 
cultural life of the county.

Library  
 
Library activity statistics 
There were 16,251 items issued in Laois Libraries in June 2026, including over 5,875 
adult items and 10,376 children's items. There were 1,355 members registered in June - 
this includes 528 new members and 827 renewing members. There were 25,410 visits to 
libraries.  There were 19,561 items loaned through the online apps BorrowBox and 
PressReader, including eBooks, audiobooks, digital newspapers, comics and magazines 
with 1,432 active users over this period. 
 
The libraries held 277 events and activities during June with 3,492 people attending these 
events. 
 
Refugee Week 
Libraries celebrated Refugee Week from 16-21 June.  This included a number of events, 
book displays and social media content to highlight the value of and challenges 
experienced by those in our community who have arrived seeking safety.  Abbeyleix 
Library held a coffee morning and library tour for the residents of the Hibernian Hotel.  
Portlaoise Library held a children’s story time and craft around kindness courage and 
friendship.  The Library Service also worked with the Integration Team on a project with 
Scoil Mhuire (Abbeyleix) and Scoil Bhríde (Portlaoise).  Classes visited Abbeyleix and 
Portlaoise Libraries for specially curated readings. These included Lantern Smoke by local 
author Dagogo Hart, and The Invisible Web by Patrice Karst. They explored themes of 
belonging, identity, kindness and connection. The children created their own Web of 
Kindness and reflected on “What makes me, me?” through self-portraits, and shared 
thoughtful ideas about how we can make others feel welcome and included.  To finish, each 
child received copies of both books to take home and keep.

Spring Summer Dance Series with Laois Offaly Rehab & Recovery in Mental Health  
 
In June 2026 the Community Dance programme initiated by Laois Arts with dance artist 
AnneKatrin Kiesel concluded for the Summer. Since its inception in Sept 2025 this 
programme has had a very positive response from Link Centre participants.  
 
AnneKatrin reported on the programme development as follows.  ‘This second block 
consisted of twelve sessions with a consistently high attendance of an average of 
eleven participants plus staff. We opened three places to participants from the Irish Wheelchair 
Association. Their participation brought fresh energy to the group and enriched the sessions. 
Having twelve sessions gave us more time to build trust. Participants gradually opened up, 
became more confident and engaged more actively and creatively with what was proposed.  
 
Feedback from participants and staff highlighted the physical, social and mental benefits of the 
sessions.  Overall, this second block strengthened my confidence as an inclusive dance facilitator 
and reinforced my belief that a structured but open environment can foster joy, well-being, 
connection and self-expression through dance.’ 
 
Laois Arts Office aims to continue developing this programme with partners at the Link 
Centre St. Fintan’s, dancer AnneKatrin and the Creative Ireland Laois team.
